rationale: Agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist, 5-HT2C antagonist; t½ ~2h; no discontinuation syndrome; no serotonergic reuptake activity) to escitalopram (SSRI). The very short half-life of agomelatine means it clears within hours — no washout period is required from agomelatine's side. Agomelatine produces no serotonin reuptake inhibition, so there is no pharmacodynamic serotonin overlap concern when starting escitalopram. Practically: agomelatine can be stopped the same day escitalopram is started. A brief overlap is used here for clinical safety and to verify tolerability. Mandatory: Check LFTs before stopping agomelatine (hepatotoxicity monitoring exit check). Contraindication note: fluvoxamine is NOT escitalopram, but ensure no CYP1A2 inhibitor is inadvertently co-prescribed during any brief overlap. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start escitalopram 10 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Check exit LFTs (ALT) — agomelatine hepatotoxicity monitoring final check. No serotonin overlap hazard: agomelatine has no serotonergic reuptake activity.
Review escitalopram tolerability (nausea, insomnia). Continue agomelatine — patient still taking nocte dose.
Stop agomelatine. Continue escitalopram 10 mg. No discontinuation syndrome expected from agomelatine (t½ ~2h). Titrate escitalopram to 20 mg after 4 weeks if inadequate response.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Agomelatine 25 mg ≈ escitalopram 10 mg (both standard effective doses for MDD). Not pharmacologically equivalent — different mechanisms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
